messages.text: MCC taking action over Lord's pitch after 'reputational blow'

metadata.summary: The MCC has outlined an action plan to address concerns over the pitch at Lord's, with it having been deemed "unsatisfactory" by the ICC.
metadata.content: Lord's pitch: MCC outlines action plan after England vs Pakistan Test to address criticism of playing surface | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content Lord's pitch: MCC outlines action plan after England vs Pakistan Test to address criticism of playing surface Lord's pitch was rated 'unsatisfactory' and given demerit point after second-shortest Test match in ground's history earlier this summer; watch the third Test between England and Pakistan, at Edgbaston, live on Sky Sports from Wednesday, September 9 Monday 31 August 2026 16:52, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eoin Morgan reacts to the MCC's proposed improvements at Lord's after concerns were raised over the quality of the pitch in recent matches The MCC has outlined an action plan to address concerns over the pitch at Lord's, with it having been deemed "unsatisfactory" by the ICC. Lord's was handed one demerit point under the ICC's Pitch and Outfield Monitoring Process after the staging of its 150th Test match between England and New Zealand earlier this summer proved to be the ground's second-shortest on record at 165 overs and two-and-a-half days' action. The playing surface was back under the spotlight this week, with stats showing that there was actually more movement on offer for bowlers during England's 194-run victory over Pakistan than in the prior Test against New Zealand. messages.text: Messi retires from international football: 'I have nothing left to give'

metadata.summary: Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international football aged 39.
metadata.content: Lionel Messi retires from international football aged 39 as Argentina's most-capped player and all-time leading goalscorer | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Breaking Lionel Messi retires from international football aged 39 as Argentina's most-capped player and all-time leading goalscorer Lionel Messi announces retirement from international football aged 39, after leading Argentina to this summer's World Cup final; Messi leaves as Argentina's most-capped and highest-scoring player, and said passing of father Jorge on August 8 had made him "more convinced" to retire Monday 31 August 2026 17:02, UK Image: Lionel Messi was in tears after Argentina's incredible comeback against Egypt at this summer's World Cup Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international football aged 39. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner, who captained his country to the World Cup in 2022, showed his enduring quality as he again led them to the final of the World Cup this summer. But 21 years on from his first appearance he has called time on his international career, leaving a record-breaking legacy of 125 goals from 207 games. No Argentine has played or scored more for their country. He retires having won every possible competition in international football, after twice winning the Copa America in 2021 and 2024, lifting the World Cup in Qatar and captaining Argentina to victory in the inaugural Finalissima in 2022. This summer, she was the first one through the door as London City Lionesses collated a star-strewn squad. The goalkeeper returns to the WSL after a two-year spell in France with PSG, something she describes as 'a very different environment'. messages.text: England's batting conundrum: Who misses out when Bethell returns?

metadata.summary: Like a finalist on TV game show Countdown, England are going to have to deal with a particularly tricky conundrum.
metadata.content: England's Test batting conundrum: Will Jordan Cox, Dan Lawrence or Emilio Gay miss out when Jacob Bethell is fit again? | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis England's Test batting conundrum: Will Jordan Cox, Dan Lawrence or Emilio Gay miss out when Jacob Bethell is fit again? England will have big decision to make in South Africa this winter when Jacob Bethell is fit again after a knee injury; Jordan Cox has impressed against Pakistan in Bethell's absence and staked claim for longer run in the side, perhaps putting pressure on opener Emilio Gay Monday 31 August 2026 13:30, UK Image: England face a batting conundrum in their Test side when Jacob Bethell returns to fitness after a knee injury Like a finalist on TV game show Countdown, England are going to have to deal with a particularly tricky conundrum. Ben Stokes' international retirement and Jacob Bethell's knee injury offered opportunities to Jordan Cox and Dan Lawrence in the Test match batting line-up and those have largely been seized, albeit against a struggling Pakistan side. While we don't think Stokes is going to make a comeback - although don't entirely rule it out - Bethell is set to return for the three-Test series in South Africa over the winter, leaving England with one batter too many for their XI.
